display.question: Stearic acid is converted into which of the following fatty acids by the enzyme Δ9 desaturase?
display.explanation:
Stearic acid is converted to oleic acid by the enzyme Δ9 desaturase.

Δ9 desaturase is present in the endoplasmic reticulum. It catalyzes the synthesis of monounsaturated fatty acids (Eg: Oleic acid) from saturated fatty acids (Eg: Stearic acid).
Δ9 desaturase is a mixed-function oxidase, requiring NADPH and O2. The first double bond is always introduced in the Δ9 positions. Humans cannot introduce double bonds beyond Δ9 positions (between C-10 and terminal methyl group). Hence, linoleic acid (Δ9,12) and linolenic acid (Δ9,12,15) are considered essential fatty acids and should be included in the diet.

display.explanation: Diffusion equilibrium for oxygen and carbon dioxide will be reached at 0.25 seconds. • Transit time: The total time the RBC takes to travel the whole pulmonary capillary = 0.75 seconds. • Air inspiration is diffused from the alveolus to the pulmonary capillary. • Diffusion equilibrium of oxygen and carbon dioxide will be reached when RBC has reached one third of transit time = (1/3) × 0.75 = 0.25 seconds. • No diffusion occurs in the remaining two thirds of the transit time.
